nn_police.text: Hoş geldiniz, welcome. Passport or ID card, please. You showed it on the other side; now you show it here. It's a very well-travelled card.
Shops, Selimiye and the Büyük Han are up Arasta. Prices are in lira, mostly. Don't faint at the noughts.

nn_dede.text: I grew up in a mixed village near Limassol. In 1963 things went bad, and for eleven years we lived in an enclave, behind sandbags, with my father on watch at night.
In 1975 we came north. My best friend at school was Greek Cypriot. I didn't see him for twenty-eight years.
When the crossings opened in 2003 he walked over with a bag of oranges from my mother's old tree. He remembered which tree. We sat in the square and didn't say anything for an hour.

nn_student.text: I study here and my best friend studies in the south. We meet for coffee in the middle of Ledra Street, more or less. It drives our parents mad, in a nice way.
My grandmother speaks Greek as well as Turkish, from the market in her village. My generation mostly speaks English to each other. Somebody should write a paper about that. Maybe me.

nn_doviz.text: Döviz means foreign exchange. Pounds into lira, lira into pounds, the day's rate, my small commission and a smile, free of charge.
